ai.description: This small, cylindrical snake reaches 30–40 cm. It is dark brown with three distinct yellow longitudinal stripes and possesses a short, spine-tipped tail. It belongs to the family Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Platyplectrurus trilineatus* is best distinguished by its three distinct, continuous longitudinal dark stripes running along the length of its otherwise pale body.
ai.habitat: The Lined Thorntail Snake inhabits high-altitude montane evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Lined Thorntail Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through loose soil in search of earthworms and other small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Platyplectrurus trilineatus* is oviparous, laying a small clutch of 3–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season in the Western Ghats of India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Lined Thorntail Snake is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at high elevations.
